endings._about: D-053: the endings and the endpoint's own checks as ONE table, its rows in the order they happen, derived from the paths' chains. The moments and the two options are my picks where the ruling left the look open (D-025.2).
endings.plain: The endings in the order they happen, read off the paths' chains: on every path an ending it checks earlier stands above one it checks later, and an ending a path checks twice stands where it is first checked. Where no path orders a pair of endings, the stage the chains show first comes first, then the handler line that reaches the ending (one raised inside a call stands at the line of that call), then its own line. The uncaught ending stands last: an error nobody catches can escape at any moment, so it has no place of its own in time.
endings.plainInput: INPUT appears twice here. FastAPI reads the body before the login check runs, so a body it cannot read ends above the gate; it checks the endpoint's own fields after the login check, so a field that does not fit ends below it.
endings.plainInputFirst: Here a field check stands above the login check: FastAPI checks a dependency's own parameters before it runs that dependency, and does not run it when one does not fit. The endpoint's own fields are checked after the login check; an ending checked at both moments stands where it is first checked.
endings.plainChecks: Each of the endpoint's own checks stands on the row of the ending it produces. A row that shared code decides (the app band, the login check, FastAPI) names who decides it, drawn apart: it is not a check the endpoint wrote, and a check a dependency makes is drawn muted beside it. A success carries no check, because it is what is left when every check passed; an uncaught ending carries none either, because no check makes it. The handler's rows split into the moments they happen at: its own checks, and what follows when a call it made raised, one group for each catch that caught it. A group names the calls that raise into its catch; a call that only runs before the catch is not named, and a group that names none still says where the error was caught.
endings.plainUnplaced: A row that starts with a check inside a call holds a check whose ending the map does not name; it stands at the line where the handler makes that call.
endings.sharedPlain: Decided by code the endpoint shares with others, not by a check of its own.
endings.rowShared: decided in code it shares with others: {v}

mo._about: His ask 2026-09-26: are the moments universal, can every block be read on them. The spine, the moment words, the reasons and the path row are my proposals (D-025.2); the two looks' defaults, moments as columns and cells as chips, are his (D-055); where each element stands is read off the feed by gen-all-endpoints.py (by_moment) and proven there.
mo.lede: One endpoint's time, left to right, with every block as a row (his default; the other look turns it). The top row names the stage each moment stands in; a column is a moment of the request; a cell holds that block's elements acting at that moment. What is true of the endpoint at no moment stands in the endpoint metadata, after the table. Pick a code in the path row to follow only that path to its ending.
how: The moments are D-053's, extended. Before the handler they are fixed: the server starting (before any request), the screen sending the request, the app's edge, FastAPI reading the body, the dependencies (the login check among them), FastAPI checking the fields. Inside the handler they are read from its own lines: its checks, and what it does among them; the work, the calls it makes after a check and before its next check, catch or commit; one moment for each catch that turns a failure into an ending; saving, its own commit. Then the answer, what happens after it, and the uncaught error last, because it can escape at any moment.

A handler moment that happens twice (checks, then a catch, then more checks) is drawn twice, in the order it happens, never merged. The excepts of one try stand side by side, then the moment the handler goes on to when nothing is raised: a request takes one of them, and a bracket over their heads says how many ways there are (in the header with a road row, that row says it). The arms of one if and else are drawn as runs in line order, though a request passes only one of them: pick its ending to see which. A fixed moment the endpoint does not have is drawn empty where it would stand.

An element stands at the moment the map records for it: its stage, its line in the handler, or the handler call it runs inside. A check stands where it is evaluated: on the paths whose chain carries it, and for a check inside a call, on the paths that make that call, less those the map shows leaving before it (on a path it rides only by the call, its hover says a path may skip it); its ending stands where the request leaves. A check the map ties only to a catch stands where that catch raises its ending. A test has no time inside the request: it rides the ending it proves. What has no moment by nature stands in the endpoint metadata; what should have a moment and the map cannot place is left in the band below, with its reason.

A step is placed once for each path it is on: with the dependencies when a dependency runs it, else at the call that path makes. So one step can stand at more than one moment: the login dependency reads a table, and a handler call reads it again. When a path's own chain names no call reaching the step, it stands at the calls the endpoint's other paths make to its function, never after that path has left.

The path: every path at once, or one path to its ending. Each path is a code, in the order its ending happens, a small gap between the moments they leave at; an ending several paths reach is several codes, told apart by the fork each takes, else by what FastAPI checks on it. A code's hover says the fork, the moment, what the ending says, its limiter, and whether it is the path in force. A picked path keeps only the moments it passes and the elements it passes there; an ending it passes by without leaving is kept.

A moment's head says little: a handler moment after a call failed names the function the map shows raising (when it names one) and the class its except takes; the checks say so; the work names the first function it calls, and how many more; saving names what the handler's own step does there. Its full name, where the catch stands and its lines are in its hover; its stage is the band above it. Clicking a head widens its column to what it holds, again gives the width back; a widened column has an edge on its head to drag, or to move with the arrow keys, between the smallest width that cuts no name and most of the box. The table opens fitted when it is wider than its box, and where even that is not enough it stays wider and slides sideways with Shift and the mouse wheel. The × hides a head, and the bar brings it back.

With one path picked, a write wears what that path does with it: saved, maybe saved, rolled back or left unsaved. An ending's status is drawn hollow when the endpoint does not declare it. A test whose status fits endings at several moments rides each of them, its chip hollow and dashed. A function behind the handler stands at the handler call that reaches it, the arrow saying how many calls below the handler it is, on the paths of the function it hangs under, less the paths the map shows leaving before it: a fork that returns, or a check that fires first, in the function that calls it (the rule a check inside a call follows); a call written inside an except stands only on the paths that enter that except. One the map reaches through no call stands where a function placed at a moment names it behind it (the Gabe Universe's behind lists), on that function's paths; its hover names any placed function whose list is cut that may also run it. One no placed function names stands in the band, and so does one that functions at different moments name. A raise called before it counts as a leaving point too, where the path's chain fires that raise or its ending was read to it. Where the map records no line the function is called at, no path can be dropped from it: on a path that leaves the function it hangs under partway, or that an error from the handler call ends with no line the map names for its raise, its hover says it may never be called there; where that function's own paths are an upper bound, its hover says so, naming the same call. A function called only inside an except the map records no path entering, while the uncaught 500 passes an error on through that except, stands in the band, on the way to the 500.

The endpoint metadata, after the table (or before it, its option), holds per block the facts no moment of a request holds: what the endpoint is (its method and path, the path it is served at, its first segment, its entity and the cluster the Gabe Universe draws it in, the station's flags, the handler's file with the line its route is declared at and the line its def stands at, its outline, its docstring) and what sums it up (how many functions stand behind it, its proof, its alarms, each path's fate, its longest path, the cases that only arrange through it, its rare pieces that name what it is, the norms it lacks), each on the card of the block it belongs to; what sums it up drawn as the pinned row draws it, under the same head word. The path row never hides it: each fact is true of every path.

A test that walks across several endpoints, a journey, keeps each of its calls here where it is, and around each one has its other requests at the outer moments of Proof: the ones it makes earlier before any request, the later ones after the answer, one chip per journey on each side (the walk in its hover) or each request a chip of its own; a call here is never drawn among them. With a path picked, a call here keeps its chips only when it ends on that path: at the ending it proves, else, for a call that arranges, at the one ending of the status it asserts; on each path to that ending, since which one it takes is not recorded. A journey whose requests cannot be set in order here is named in the endpoint metadata, on Proof's card, with its reason: a group of web or end-to-end cases whose report is not read, a test with no record of its requests, one that records one request, one none of whose recorded requests calls this endpoint, or one whose every request calls it.

road.plain: A row of stages; under it the road, whether the moments below come in turn or are ways a request takes one of; then the moments.

save._about: D-068, his L-05: the stage the handler's own save stands in. Both are my proposal; saving under EFFECTS is my pick, dashed, so every stage the station draws has a moment.
save.label: saving

eff.name: saving under EFFECTS
eff.plain: The handler's own commit stands under EFFECTS, the writes it leaves behind, after the handler's other moments.

hand.name: saving under HANDLER
hand.plain: The handler's own commit stays under HANDLER, the handler's code; EFFECTS is drawn as an empty outline beside it.

meta._about: D-068, his L-06 ("separate from the table at the end. Or at the beginning"): where the endpoint metadata stands. After the table, his first words, is yours: ruled in his review of round 1.
meta.label: the metadata

after.name: metadata after the table
after.plain: The endpoint metadata stands under the table, before what the map cannot place.

before.name: metadata before the table
before.plain: The endpoint metadata stands above the table, under the bar.

wid._about: D-068, his L-21 ("click the columns for accommodation … give a little more width to put the contents as is expected"): what a click on a head gives its column. Both are my proposal; every item on one line is yours, ruled in his review of round 1 over my names whole.
wid.label: a head's click

names.name: names whole
names.plain: Clicking a moment's head widens its column until no name inside breaks in the middle of a word; a name still breaks after its _ . / or at a space.

line.name: every item on one line
line.plain: Clicking a moment's head widens its column until every item inside stands on one line.

fit._about: D-068, his L-21 ("a button that will force accommodation by minimizing or moving the other columns around"): what the fit button does. Both are my proposal; wrapping into bands is yours, ruled in his review of round 1 over my narrowing the rest.
fit.label: fit

min.name: narrow the rest
min.plain: The fit button narrows the columns that do not fit, the ones with fewest items first, to a strip where each cell says how many items it holds; click a strip to widen it. A widened column keeps its width.

bands.name: wrap into bands
bands.plain: The fit button wraps the table into bands of moments that fit the box, one under the other: time runs left to right, then down.

gdl._about: D-069, his L-10 ("we will most likely mutate that to have a chain of functions with the actual gates and decisions … and then the effect of that"): how a gate's chain function → condition → effect is drawn. All three are my proposal (D-025.2); the function as a head with its gates under it is yours, ruled in his review of round 1.
gdl.label: the gates

chain.name: one chain per gate
chain.plain: Each gate is one chip: the function it runs in, then its condition, then what happens. The function repeats on each of its gates.

head.name: function, gates under it
head.plain: The function each gate runs in is a head, with its gates under it, one line each: condition, then what happens.

cols.name: function · condition · effect
cols.plain: Each gate is a row of parts side by side, function, condition and what happens, so the effects line up.

gef._about: D-069, his L-10 ("we should encode that with some color … for that branch or the stage"): how a gate's effect is coloured. Both are my proposal; the ending's own colour with the stage lit is yours, ruled in his review of round 1.
gef.label: the effect

end.name: ending's colour, stage lit
end.plain: The effect is the ending's status in its own colour, and a small spine of the stages with the one it leaves from lit.

stage.name: a colour per stage
stage.plain: The effect is the ending's status on a band in the colour of the stage it leaves from.

gic._about: D-069, his L-09: the station draws no node for a gate, so a gate wears this page's own icon. An icon per kind is yours, ruled in his review of round 1.
gic.label: gate icons

each.name: an icon per kind
each.plain: A rate limit, a check, a fork, a catch and a switch each wear an icon of their own.

one.name: one gate icon
one.plain: Every gate wears the same icon; the label at its end tells them apart.

none.name: no icon
none.plain: A gate wears no icon, as before.

grl._about: D-069, his L-11 ("can we also put some roles in the gates and decisions themselves? … they validate things on different levels"): the label at a gate's end. Where it decides is yours, ruled in his review of round 1.
grl.label: gate roles

where.name: where it decides
where.plain: The label says where the gate decides: app-wide, at login, in a dependency, in the handler, or inside a call.

what.name: what it does
what.plain: The label says what the gate does: refuses, translates, routes, passes on or swallows.

guards.name: what it guards
guards.plain: A check's label says what its refusal means: bad input, not found, conflict and so on; other gates wear none.

fnm._about: D-069 (lost-columns P2, his L-20 and L-12): a function chip shows what gets it counted in the pinned row. Showing them is yours, ruled in his review of round 1.
fnm.label: function marks

on.name: what it decides and touches
on.plain: A function shows the statuses its own code decides, and R or W for each table it reads or writes here; the login check's own tables are hollow.

off.name: name and role only
off.plain: A function shows its name and role only.

std._about: D-069, his L-18 ("I'm not sure what we are representing here … maybe merged with gates and decisions … tell me about that"): where Standard or specialist's items stand. All three are my proposal; splitting it is yours, ruled in his review of round 1. In each, the row's head says the question it answers.
std.label: standard or specialist

split.name: split into the gates
split.plain: A switch stands in Gates and decisions beside what it switches, marked set by settings; a rare piece becomes a label at the end of the item it names. The row leaves the table.

merge.name: merge into the gates
merge.plain: Every item of the row stands in Gates and decisions as it is. The row leaves the table.

keep.name: keep the row
keep.plain: The row stays, in lanes: what the server's settings switch, and what is rare here.

dfx._about: D-070, his L-12 ("put functions … in blocks … on the left, and in the right the tables, and have sort of a mind map … where the connectors will describe the kind of operation … we are affecting these tables, but how? With what function?"): how Data effects shows which function does what to which table. The chips are what stood there; the two maps are my proposal; a small map per moment is yours, ruled in his review of round 1 over my one map for the endpoint. The colours are the page's own read and write colours.
dfx.label: data effects

chips.name: chips
chips.plain: One chip per read or write at its moment: the table and R or W; the function in its hover.

cell.name: a small map per moment
cell.plain: Inside each moment's cell: its functions on the left, its tables on the right, a line from each function to each table it touches, in the read or the write colour (the option "write colour").

one.name: one map for the endpoint
one.plain: Under the row, full width: the functions on the left in the order they first touch data, the tables on the right in the order they are first touched, the moments as bands from top to bottom. A line in the read colour reads, one in the write colour writes (the option "write colour"); a function that reads a table and then writes it gets both, in that order. A tick is a flush; a rule across is a commit and names who commits. With the map on, the row's cells only say how many; the map draws each read and write once. A picked path dims what it does not run.

dxc._about: Round-1 review S4-29, his L-12 words "write red, read green": the colours of a read and a write, in the Data effects chips and its map. He also said "I think that somehow we have already encoded that": the page's own colours (read green, write orange, both amber) are yours, ruled in his review of round 1; his words' colours are the other option.
dxc.label: write colour

page.name: the page's colours
page.plain: Read green, write orange, both amber: the colours the page already gives R and W, beside the station's red for a function that touches the store.

his.name: his words' colours
his.plain: Write red, read green, both orange: the colours he named. Red is also the colour of the station's accessor label beside a function.

jyb._about: Review CR-20: where a test's earlier requests stand — the review offered both places; yours, ruled in his review of round 1: a moment of their own.
jyb.label: a test's earlier requests

prior.name: their own moment
prior.plain: Earlier in the test: a moment of their own before this request is sent, apart from the server starting.

head.name: in Proof's head
head.plain: In the Proof row's head, out of the moments: a test's earlier requests are no time of this request.

stk._about: Review CR-07: what the heads do while BY MOMENT scrolls past the pinned row — the review offered heads that ride down or a folded pin; yours, ruled in his review of round 1: the heads ride down.
stk.label: the heads, scrolled

ride.name: ride under the pinned row
ride.plain: The stage band and the moment heads ride down under the pinned row while the table scrolls past, so the pinned row's heads are never read as BY MOMENT's.

stay.name: stay at the top
stay.plain: The heads stay at the table's top; scrolled down, only the pinned row's heads are in view.

ifl._about: D-070, his L-17 ("visualize or surface what we are affecting … dig deeper … possibilities"): how In-flight state shows what each value affects. The chips are what stood there; lifelines and echoes are my proposal; a lifeline each is yours, ruled in his review of round 1.
ifl.label: in-flight values

chips.name: chips where set
chips.plain: One chip per value, at the moment it is set.

lane.name: a lifeline each
lane.plain: One lane per value across the moments: its chip where it is set, a line while it lives, a dot where it is read with what that read can decide, a cross at the answer — or an arrow on past it when the server keeps it. Values set together and read alike fold into one lane that opens.

echo.name: echoes where read
echo.plain: The chip stays where the value is set; a small echo stands at each moment that reads it, with what that read can decide.

secmv._about: D-084, his L-19 (ruled G2, a row of its own): the security facts that already stand in other rows — the 401 and 429 endings, the limiters, the row the login adds, the login check, the repeat key. Where they stand is a choice made alone, so it is an option; the marks were my pick (dashed) until he ruled them in D-085 ("use recommended approach on pending decision"): a short mark to the home row.
secmv.label: security facts that live elsewhere

marks.name: marks to their home row
marks.plain: A short mark in Security names each such fact and the row that holds it; the fact stays in its own row, in full. Click a mark to go there.

moved.name: moved into Security
moved.plain: Each such fact leaves its row and stands here, in full. The row it came from no longer draws it.

secmw._about: D-085, his L-19 (the Security row): a middleware that hosts a switch stood twice at the edge — as its numbered chip in the run order, and again as the head of the card that holds its switch (the rate limit middleware on POST /cooking/sessions). One element, one place: merged draws the middleware once, its numbered chip with the switch inside it (my pick, dashed: D-085 leaves it his); apart keeps the chip and the card as the row drew them. It holds for any middleware that hosts a switch, on every endpoint.
secmw.label: a middleware with its switch

merged.name: switch inside its middleware
merged.plain: A middleware that hosts a switch is drawn once, as its numbered chip in the run order, with the switch inside it.

apart.name: chip and card apart
apart.plain: The numbered chip stands in the run order, and the switch stands in a card headed by the same middleware's name, as the row drew it before.

stg._about: D-068, his L-05: the stage band over the moments. Which stage each moment stands in is gen-all-endpoints.py's (MO_STAGE, proven against each ending's stage); the words, the numbering and the bracket are my proposal.
stg.head: stage

out.name: outside the request
out.plain: Not a stage of the request: the server starting before any request, a test's earlier requests, the screen that sends it, and what happens once the answer has left.

stg.partPlain: The request comes back to this stage later: this is part {i} of {k}, in time order.

why.INPUT: FastAPI reads the body before the dependencies run, and checks the fields after them.

eff.name: EFFECTS
eff.plain: In this look the handler's own save stays under HANDLER, so EFFECTS has no moment of its own: the writes land inside the handler's moments, and the Data effects row shows them.

fork.name: one of {n} ways
fork.plain: A request takes one of these {n} ways: an except of this try turns the error its call raised into an ending, or nothing is raised and the handler goes on.
fork.none: this path takes none of them: it leaves before the try, or its error escapes

road.head: road
road.seqPlain: These moments come one after another; a request can end at any of them.

col._about: D-068, his L-21: the columns' controls. Their words are my proposal; what widening and fit do are options (mo.opt.wid, mo.opt.fit).
col.hidePlain: Hide this moment; the bar keeps it, to bring it back.
col.hideRowPlain: Hide this row; the bar keeps it, to bring it back.
col.fitPlain: Make the table fit its box, the way the squares beside it say; again to turn it off.
col.widen: Click: widen this column to what it holds; again: give the width back.
col.mini: Narrowed to fit: each cell says how many items it holds. Click to widen it.
col.edgePlain: Drag this edge left or right, or focus it and press the arrow keys (Shift for a bigger step). The column keeps a width no name is cut at, and no more than most of the box; click the head to give the width back.

rowh._about: D-068, his L-20 ("those are interesting pieces that I would like to see reflected here"): a row's head repeats its block's columns of the pinned row, with the same head words and this endpoint's values. The options slot holds what is the row's alone. Both are my proposal.
rowh.light: Click: light what this column counts, here and in its cell of the pinned row; again: turn it off.

jy._about: D-065, his ruling 2026-09-28 ("build A and B"): a journey's other requests at the outer moments of Proof, and the journeys that cannot be ordered named in the endpoint metadata. The two looks, the chip's words and the hover are my proposal (D-025.2): one chip per journey per side of each call it makes here is my pick (review J1: each call here has its own pair). Which journeys, their steps, the path join and the reasons are read and proven by gen-all-endpoints.py (by_moment).
jy.head: {cid} · a journey
jy.sideB: its requests up to this one, in order:
jy.sideA: its requests from this one on, in order:
jy.hereAgain: {i} · this endpoint, another call, with chips of its own · {role}
jy.noEp: no endpoint of the app matches it
jy.on: its request on this endpoint ends in {v}
jy.onEach: the test does not show which of the ways to that ending it takes

leave.none: this request asserts no status: the test does not show how it ends
leave.miss: this request asserts {v}, which no ending of this endpoint answers
leave.many: this request asserts {v}, which {n} endings of this endpoint answer: the test does not show which one it gets
leave.act: this request acts and asserts {v}; the test does not show which ending it gets

jy.plain: A journey is a test that calls this endpoint and others, one after another. Each of its calls here stays where it is: the proof at its ending, or its line among the cases that arrange through it. Around each one its other requests stand: the earlier ones earlier in the test, the later ones after the answer. With a path picked, a call here keeps its chips when it ends on that path: at the ending it proves, else, for a call that arranges, at the one ending of the status it asserts; on each path to that ending, since which one it takes is not recorded.
jy.feed: Journeys: the Gabe Universe names {jyRows} across the page's endpoints, on {jyEps} of them, and counts {jyMore} more on {jyMoreEps} of them that it does not name. {jyOrd} walk across their endpoint and others and stand at the outer moments, around each of the {jyCalls} calls they make to it: with a path picked, {jyRefs} of those calls keep their chips by the ending the call proves, {jyStat} by the one ending of the status it asserts, and {jyNone} leave. The rest are named in the endpoint metadata, on Proof's card with the reason: {jyAgg} groups of web or end-to-end cases whose report is not read, {jyNoRec} tests with no record of their requests, {jyOne} that record one request, {jyNoHere} none of whose recorded requests calls their endpoint, and {jyOnly} whose every request calls it.

band.title: not placed
band.plain: What should have a moment and has no known one, each with its reason. What has no moment by nature stands in the endpoint metadata, beside the journeys whose requests cannot be set in order around this one.
band.all: every element that should have a moment has one

nm._about: D-064 (2), his ruling 2026-09-28: the facts no moment holds, per block. D-068, his ruling 2026-09-30 (L-06, L-07): out of the table, into the endpoint metadata, one card per block. Its place (after the table, my pick; before it, its option), its name and these words are my proposal; which facts stand there, and on which block's card, is read from the ruled tree's homes by gen-all-endpoints.py (no_moment) and proven there. `only` names the blocks whose every fact has no moment.
nm.name: endpoint metadata
nm.plain: Facts with no moment: what the endpoint is and what sums it up, one card per block. Each is true of every path, so the path row never hides it; and, on Proof's card, the journeys whose requests cannot be set in order around this one, each with its reason.

ep.name: method and path
ep.plain: The verb and the URL a client calls.

full.name: the path it is served at
full.plain: The path the app answers it on: its own path, with its router's mount before it.

seg.name: the URL's first segment
seg.plain: The first part of its path: the group of URLs it sits in.
seg.label: its route is written as {v}; the app serves it at the longer path

ent.name: entity
ent.plain: The feature of the app that owns the endpoint.

cl.name: cluster
cl.plain: The group of related endpoints it sits in, inside its entity.
cl.label: its route is written as {v}

risk.name: flag
risk.plain: A warning about the endpoint's code.

untested.name: no test calls it
untested.plain: No test calls the endpoint: no case acts on it and none sets another test up through it.

conflict.name: large surface
conflict.plain: Many functions stand behind the handler, or many pieces lead to it, so a change here reaches far.

god.name: oversized handler
god.plain: Its handler is one of the app's oversized functions or classes.

behind.name: functions behind
behind.plain: How many functions the handler's own calls reach, and how many calls below it the deepest one stands; the functions its dependencies run are not counted (the Functions row draws them at the moment the dependencies run).

proof.name: proof
proof.plain: How many of the endings its code produces a test names (every ending but the answer and the body's parse errors; a test whose status fits several endings counts for each, and so does a test of the same error raised in another function), and where that puts the endpoint among the app's.

alarm.name: alarm
alarm.plain: Something in the code that looks wrong; each alarm's hover says what it found here.

says._about: review F11 · S4-09 · CR-21: what each alarm found on THIS endpoint, its values read from the alarm's own record (alarm_words in gen-all-endpoints.py); race-500 says the one race sentence, mo.x.race
says.textOnly: {n} of its refusals send words only, and no code a client could tell them apart by
says.undeclared: it answers {v}, and its route declares none of them
says.collapsed: {fn} shows the same message for {v}: a user cannot tell them apart
says.lost: at {at} the {st} answers “{v}”, while the error it caught said “{was}”: the first reason is lost
says.escape: {cls}, raised at {at}, is caught by no except: the request ends in {st}
says.refWrites: {n} of its ways to a refusal still save a write
says.safeCommits: it commits at {v}, though a {m} request should change nothing

file.name: the handler's file and line
file.plain: The file the handler lives in, and the line its route is declared at: its decorator, which stands above the def. The line the def stands at is beside it when it is known.

sig.name: the handler's outline
sig.plain: Async or not, how many lines it runs, the type it returns; its def in the hover.

doc.name: the handler's docstring
doc.plain: The text the handler's author wrote at its top.

fate.name: each path's fate
fate.plain: What becomes of the endpoint's own writes, path by path, counted: saved, maybe saved, rolled back, left unsaved, after the answer, or no write of its own.

chain.name: the longest path
chain.plain: How many steps the longest path a request can take runs through.

arr.name: arranges another test
arr.plain: A case that calls this endpoint only to set another test up. A test has no time inside the request, and this one proves no ending of this endpoint.
arr.plainAct: A case that calls this endpoint to test it, and calls it again to set a later request up. Its testing calls stand in the Proof row, at the ending each proves, or among the calls that prove no ending.

jy.name: a journey not ordered
jy.plain: A test that calls this endpoint among other requests; the test does not show when, among them, it calls this one.
jy.col: Its requests happen at moments like any request's; it stands here because the test does not show their order around this one.

agg.name: no requests listed
agg.plain: A group of cases from the {corpus} tests; their report lists no requests.

one.name: no walk
one.plain: The test makes {n} request(s), so there is nothing to set around this one.

norec.name: no requests listed
norec.plain: The test's requests are not written down.

nohere.name: no call here
nohere.plain: None of the requests the test makes calls this endpoint.

only.name: only here
only.plain: Every request the test makes calls this endpoint, so there is no other endpoint to walk to.

piece.name: a rare piece
piece.plain: A piece few endpoints carry that names what the endpoint is (its method, its login, its limit), not something that acts.

lack.name: a norm it lacks
lack.plain: A piece nearly every endpoint carries that this one does not.

nolink.name: no known call to it
nolink.plain: No call the handler makes is known to lead to it, so when it happens in the request is not known.

twomom.name: calls at different moments
twomom.plain: It is reached from handler calls made at different moments.

notable.name: the step is not known
notable.plain: The endpoint reads or writes this table, and which of its steps does it is not known.

firstcall.name: filled on a first call
firstcall.plain: Its value is built by whichever request calls it first, and no one can say which.

spans.name: several moments
spans.plain: The endings it stands for leave at several moments, so it has no single one.

member.name: a member has no moment
member.plain: It stands for endings or catches, and one of them has no moment of its own.

noend.name: proves no ending
noend.plain: The test sends the request but none of its assertions fits an ending.

nosite.name: outside the handler
nosite.plain: It sits at a line outside the handler's own code, and no call the handler makes is known to lead to it.

pathsonly.name: place on its paths not known
pathsonly.plain: Which paths pass it is known, but not where on them.

fnnone.name: reached by no known call
fnnone.plain: The function is named, and no handler call is known to reach it.

swmoves.name: moves with the path
swmoves.plain: On different paths it happens at different moments.

nopath.name: on no path
nopath.plain: It belongs to the endpoint, but none of its paths passes it, so no path can be followed to it.

noname.name: no single function by this name
noname.plain: No single function in the code carries this name, so no call can be followed to it, and no function at a moment of this request reaches it by that name.

in500.name: on the way to the 500
in500.plain: It is called inside an except that passes the error on, and every known way into that except ends in the uncaught 500.

mo.scrolls: The table is wider than its box: slide it sideways with Shift and the mouse wheel, or with the scroll bar.

io._about: D-067 (his rulings on L-01 to L-04 and L-22): ONE hover per BY MOMENT item, its own facts in the order the code meets them. before: what must already hold, and what brings the code here. checks: what it checks or does, and where. gives: what comes out of it and what that does. The generator writes each line from a record of the feed (_ae_io.io_of) and names its words here (a key of `l`, or of mo.x for a line the page already had); a part the feed holds nothing for is left out. What a KIND means is not in an item's hover: it stands once, in the row's legend (`k`, and the chips' own words).

guard.plain: A check the endpoint's own code makes; when it holds, the request ends.

fork.plain: A branch whose arms lead the request different ways.

catch.plain: An except: an error raised below is caught here and turned into an answer, or let through.

limiter.plain: A rate limit: it counts a caller's requests over a window and refuses the one past the limit.

login.plain: The dependency that reads the caller's credential and decides who the caller is.

clfn.name: screen function
clfn.plain: A function of the screen's code that reads the answer and picks what the screen shows.

table.plain: A read or a write on a table.

step.name: save step
step.plain: A flush, a commit or a rollback: where the session's writes go to the database, or are undone.

fn.plain: A function the request runs through.

body.name: request body
body.plain: The schema FastAPI reads the request's body into.

field.name: body field
field.plain: One field of the request body, with the rules FastAPI checks on it.

reply.name: reply
reply.plain: The schema the answer's body is built from.

schema.plain: A schema inside the body or the reply.

hook.name: hook
hook.plain: The frontend code that sends this request.

file.plain: A frontend file that sends this request.

screen.name: screen
screen.plain: A screen above the code that sends this request.

cache.name: cache write
cache.plain: What the screen does to its cached data once the answer comes back.

reason.plain: A branch of the screen's code that reads the answer and does something with it.

inflight.plain: A value alive while the request runs: where it is set, where it is read, how long it lasts.

switch.plain: A setting or a binding that changes what the request does.

piece.plain: Something this endpoint has that few others have.

mw.name: middleware
mw.plain: Code that runs on every request before the endpoint, in the order the app registers it.

rule.plain: A rule FastAPI checks on the input; when it fails, the answer is a 422.

case.plain: A test that calls this endpoint, and the ending it proves.

journey.name: journey
journey.plain: A test that calls this endpoint and others, one after another; its chip stands for its requests before this one, or after it.

jstep.name: journey step
jstep.plain: One request a journey makes to another endpoint, in its place in the walk.

built.name: a class it builds
built.plain: A class the code builds here: a schema or a model, not a function.

rest.name: any other status
rest.plain: The endings a client function has no branch for: none of its comparisons matches them.

orch.name: hook on the way
orch.plain: Frontend code between the screen and the hook that sends the request: it calls that hook and takes its errors.

cors.name: allowed origins
cors.plain: The websites the CORS middleware lets call the API from a browser: the default the code gives, and what an example env file sets instead.

secret.name: secret
secret.plain: A setting that holds a secret and is read on this request's way. Its value is never shown here.

secmark.name: mark
secmark.plain: A security fact that stays in its own row, in full. The mark names it and the row that holds it; click it to go there.

outcome.swallow: swallows the error: the code goes on

l.corsAllow: lets these websites call the API, by default: {v}
l.corsGuard: checked when the app starts, by {fn}
l.corsEnv: an example env file sets it to {v}
l.corsEnvC: an example env file names {v}, commented out
l.secEnvdefined: an example env file defines it; the value is not shown
l.secEnvexternal: an example env file names it, commented out; the value is not shown
l.secEnvdefault: no example env file sets it; the code's default stands
l.limScope: on paths that start with one of {n} prefixes: {v}
l.limCheck: {via} keeps each caller's count for its {lim} limit, and answers when the count is over, at {at}
l.limIp: {n} per {w} seconds, counted per caller IP, apart for the {v} limit
l.limIp1: {n} per {w} seconds, counted per caller IP

A list carries each of its items apart: an alarm when every fact it reads stands at its moment, a path's fate when its writes wear it on its pick (or it writes nothing of its own). A count is carried when every member it counts is placed, in part when some are. A field that sums the whole endpoint up (the count of the fates, the alarms' dots, the longest chain, the count behind, the proof's rank) is carried by BY MOMENT's endpoint metadata, which draws it; so is what the endpoint is there (its entity, the handler's file, the cases that only arrange through it, the norms it lacks). Where BY MOMENT's steps touch tables the code map does not list, the tables fields stay in every look and say how many, and the header counts them.

REUSE FIRST — `col`/`ico`/`txt` name where a family's colour, icon and chip text are read: `table` = the page's own tokens and classes (the endings slots --k-*, the stage spine, the fate stack --f-*, the pieces stack --p-*, the method colours --m-*, the alarm dots' --alert, the validation slot's colour); `lab` = the endpoint lab's source, cut out of _lab-ep-panels.js and run under node with the station's tokens by gen-all-endpoints.py (the channel chip R · W · RW and its .jdrw rule in _lab-ep.css, the five path kinds' glyphs, the status colour rule — the lab colours a 3xx as it colours a 5xx, kept as the lab has it — the in-flight kinds' glyphs and lifetime tones, the direction chip IN · OUT, the words for what a branch does); `station` = the Gabe Universe's own encoding (D-052): a family an element wears as its subcategory (method · role · hook role · component, module and provider class · delivery) is the station's badge colour and word, lifted from gabe-universe.html by _ae_universe.station_kinds; the entity is the station's entity glyph in that entity's colour. A finding's hover words are the forms registry's own (_a3_forms.py FINDINGS). `mine` = MY PROPOSAL, for a family nothing encodes yet: an icon per value from the station's own icon set, and no new colour. `rule.groups[*].keywords` sorts the 422 rule types by the Field keyword that makes each (the short arm's PYDANTIC_ERRORS), `table` by the short arm's MODEL_ERRORS / RAISE_ERRORS — which group a keyword belongs to is my proposal; a keyword no group names stops the build.

rw.name: reads and writes
rw.plain: The endpoint reads this table and writes it.

1.name: an informational status
1.plain: The server says it is still working on the request.

3.name: a redirect status
3.plain: The caller is sent somewhere else.

4.name: a client error status
4.plain: The request is refused; the caller can change it and try again.

5.name: a server error status
5.plain: The server failed; nothing the caller changes fixes it.

ifk.name: kind of in-flight value
ifk._about: D-069, his L-17 ("give it an appropriate icon … a better representation with some icon coloring"): each kind its own glyph and a plain label at the chip's end, replacing the feed's machine word; one hue for the row, the lifetime by the chip's fill. My proposal (D-025.2), not the lab's catalogue.

state.name: on the request
state.plain: Kept on the request itself, for code later in the same request to read.

contextvar.name: in context
contextvar.plain: A context value the code reads without it being passed along.

dependency-value.name: from a dependency
dependency-value.plain: Handed to the handler by one of its dependencies.

background.name: after the answer
background.plain: Queued to run once the answer has been sent.

lock.name: held
lock.plain: Held by this request so no other request can take it at the same time.

cache.name: cached
cache.plain: An answer kept from an earlier request and reused.

built-once.name: built at start
built-once.plain: Built once when the server starts; every request uses the same one.

setting-once.name: setting at start
setting-once.plain: A setting read once when the server starts; every request uses that value.

ent.name: entity
ent.plain: The entity that claims this endpoint, with the entity glyph in its own colour, as the Gabe Universe draws an entity.

binding.plain: Which implementation is plugged in decides the way.

value.plain: A setting's value decides the way.

flag.plain: A flag turns a way on or off.

branch.name: what the branch does with the reason

reads.plain: The branch reads the reason the endpoint gives.

passed.plain: The branch hands the error to code that reads it.

value.plain: The branch only picks a value.

none.plain: It decides by the status alone; the words the server sent are not read.

unread.plain: What the branch does is not read: its condition is too long.

_other.plain: What the branch does with the reason.

read.plain: What the branch runs is known, row by row.

mixed.plain: More than one check on a line shares these rows.

pattern.name: a pattern the text must match

model.name: a rule of the whole shape: a field required, a field not allowed, a value from a list

validator.name: a rule the app's own validator raises

limit.plain: It lets this many requests through per window, then refuses.

gdk.name: kind of gate

l.plain: It counts a caller's requests over a window and refuses the one past the limit.

g.plain: A condition in the code; when it holds, the request ends.

a.plain: The dependency that reads the caller's credential and decides who the caller is.

b.plain: A branch whose arms send the request different ways.

c.plain: An except: an error raised below is caught here and turned into an answer, or let through.

w.plain: A setting or a plugged-in part, set by the server's settings, that changes a way the request can go.

one.name: gate
one.plain: A place where the code decides: a limit, a check, a fork or a catch.

gdl.name: where it decides
gdl._about: D-069, his L-11 ("since they validate things on different levels"): R2, read from the gate's host — the app's middleware, the login dependency, another dependency, the handler's own code, or a function it calls. My proposal.

app.name: app-wide
app.plain: In the app's middleware, before any endpoint's own code runs.

login.name: at login
login.plain: In the login check, while FastAPI works out who the caller is.

dep.name: in a dependency
dep.plain: In one of the endpoint's dependencies, before the handler runs.

call.name: inside a call
call.plain: In a function the handler calls.

gdv.name: what it does
gdv._about: D-069, his L-11: R1, read from the gate's kind and a catch's outcome. My proposal.

refuses.name: refuses
refuses.plain: When its condition holds, the request ends with a refusal.

translates.name: translates
translates.plain: It turns an error raised below into an answer.

routes.name: routes
routes.plain: It picks which answer the request gets.

passes.name: passes on
passes.plain: It catches an error and raises it again, to an outer catch.

swallows.name: swallows
swallows.plain: It catches an error and the code goes on as if nothing happened.

gdc.name: what it guards
gdc._about: D-069, his L-11: R3, a check's refusal by what its status means (checks only). My proposal.

400.name: bad input
400.plain: The request is missing something or says something the code will not take.

402.name: payment needed
402.plain: The caller's plan does not cover this.

403.name: forbidden
403.plain: The caller is known but may not do this.

404.name: not found
404.plain: What the request names does not exist, or is not the caller's.

409.name: conflict
409.plain: The request clashes with what the server already holds.

413.name: too large
413.plain: The request is bigger than the code allows.

415.name: wrong type
415.plain: The request's content is of a type the code does not take.

422.name: invalid
422.plain: A value breaks a rule the code checks.

429.name: too many
429.plain: The caller has asked too often.

502.name: upstream failed
502.plain: A service the code calls answered badly.

503.name: unavailable
503.plain: Something the code needs is not available now.

_other.name: refusal
_other.plain: The request ends with this status.

gef.name: what happens
gef._about: D-069, his L-10 ("the result of that is an ending or maybe something else … maybe a branching"): the word between a gate's condition and its effect. My proposal.

ends.name: ends
ends.plain: When the condition holds, the request ends with this answer.

ret.name: returns
ret.plain: The function returns here, and the request goes on to this answer.

pass.name: passes the error on
pass.plain: The error is raised again, to a catch further out or to the uncaught error.

goes.name: goes on
goes.plain: The error is swallowed and the code goes on.

dec.name: decides
dec.plain: Its setting decides whether these endings can happen.

can.name: can end at
can.plain: Whichever part is plugged in, the request can end the same way.

station.title: what the Gabe Universe draws
station.plain: An element the Gabe Universe draws as a node wears its glyph there, in its colour there; a label at the end names its subcategory, in the colour of the badge the station hangs on that node. Point at a glyph or a label for its words. Which of this page's kinds are drawn as which of the station's is my proposal where they are not the same:
station.drawn: as the Gabe Universe draws its node
station.drawnEnt: as the Gabe Universe names an entity
station.glyph: The glyph and the colour this kind of element wears in the Gabe Universe.
station.alias: The Gabe Universe names this setting as one of the flag's aliases, so it is that flag and wears the flag's glyph.
station.card: This is the node's look. The universe column copies the station's card, whose chips and entity faces use the card's own colours, so the same element can look different there: the station differs from itself.
station.nonode: The Gabe Universe draws no node for this function; it wears the function glyph all the same, and its role where one is known.

station.not: Not drawn by the Gabe Universe as a node, so each keeps this page's own look: {v}.

flag.why: The station's feature flag node, where its map holds the flag.

table.why: A table and its model class are one element here (D-041); the station draws the model, where its map holds one for the table.

file.why: The station draws a file as a node only when no entity claims it; any other file is no node.

guard.why: An own guard is a condition inside the handler; the station draws the endpoint's gates as its Guards list, never as a node.

setting.why: A setting is a value a condition reads; the station draws a node only for a feature flag. A setting the station names as one of a flag's aliases is that flag, and wears the flag's glyph.

limiter.why: A rate limiter lives inside the rate-limit middleware, which the station draws as one node for every request.

case.why: A test case sits on the card's Tests row, not as a node.

status.why: A status is a value, not a node.

fork.why: A deciding branch is a place in the code, not a node.

catch.why: A catch is a place in the code, not a node.

switch.why: A switch is what decides a way; the station draws none.

reason.why: A reason site is a line of a screen, not a node.

rule.why: A validation rule sits on a field of a schema, not as a node.

inflight.why: A value alive during a request is not a node.

finding.why: A finding is a fact about the endpoint, not a node.

piece.why: A piece is how common a shape is across the endpoints, not a node.

ex._about: D-071 (his L-23 · L-08 · L-13 · L-11): the examples bench — one column per kind of element, in his order, each an example drawn as a block with its controls below it. The table's look is his DATA line (D-027); the schema's and the function's boot on the lab's looks, which is my choice (dashed); the other five kinds' parts and looks are my picks, dashed. Where BY MOMENT already has words for a thing (an in-flight value's kind, how long it lives, a gate's kind and where it decides, a race, the three parts of a hover, the reply), the bench reads those words, never a copy.
ex.title: examples
ex.lede: One example of each kind of element this page draws, a column each, in the order a request meets them: an ending, a table, a schema, a function, a test, a gate or decision, a client hook, an in-flight value. Pick the element at the top of a column, narrow it by its role, set the column's width, and change what its block shows with the controls under it.
ex.how: A block reads top to bottom: its title lines, then a strip of marks — a table's or a schema's fields, the tables a function touches, the requests a test makes, the checks on an ending's way, what a gate waits for, the endings a hook answers, the places a value is read — then a list that opens when you click the block. Its hover says what comes before it, what it checks and what it gives, in the form BY MOMENT's hovers option picks. A block hovers by part: its glyph and the pill that classifies it give one card about what the element is and what that class means for it, its title gives the whole card, and each place it names (a file, a where, a class, a setter) and each mark of the strip give a card of their own. A mark of a field is paler when the column can be null (a schema's: when the field may be left out) and carries a corner at its top right and its bottom left when a unique key names it; a line under the block says so, with how many. A function's, a test's or an ending's marks can carry one more yes or no the feed records: an option under the block, off until it is chosen, my pick dashed. Above each block, icon squares (point at one for what it does): the elements of this endpoint or of every endpoint (one not on the open endpoint is drawn as it is on the first endpoint that has it), and the width of the element drawn there — dynamic, shorter, compact, most compact, the column's box keeping its size; the chips narrow the column to one role and the arrows step through the elements. Under each block, always in view: the parts to drag between the lines or into not drawn, their sizes and the colours; the squares at the bottom put the block back on its first look and copy its settings as one line, to paste back with your words.

gate.plain: A place in the code that checks something and decides what happens next.

hook.name: client hook
hook.plain: The piece of the web app that calls this endpoint.

inf.name: in-flight value
inf.plain: A value that is alive while the request runs.

row.name: one row across the page
row.plain: Every kind side by side, left to right; each column keeps the width a name needs, and the row scrolls sideways when the page is narrower.

wrap.name: wrapped rows
wrap.plain: The columns wrap onto a new row when the page runs out of width.

half.name: an upper and a lower row
half.plain: The first half of the kinds on top, the second half below.

on.name: follow it
on.plain: Clicking an element in ONE ENDPOINT or BY MOMENT shows it in its kind's column, when the column holds it.

off.name: stay
off.plain: The columns keep the element you picked.

here.name: this endpoint
here.plain: The elements of the endpoint the table has open.

all.name: every endpoint
all.plain: Every element of this kind on any endpoint. One that is not on the open endpoint is drawn as it is on the first endpoint that has it.

width._about: L-36, his words "Dynamic width - Full width - A shorter width - A compact width - The most compact version", then D-087, his words "the full width is something we are not going to use": the width of the element drawn at the top of each column of the bench — only that element, never the column's box, so the grid keeps its size. Full is gone; a saved or copied full reads as the default. Dynamic, the column's own size, is my pick, dashed; the other three are his. Kept per viewer, and part of the column's copy line.
width.label: width

dynamic.name: dynamic
dynamic.plain: The element fills its column: the column keeps the share of the row its layout gives it, and the element grows with it.

shorter.name: shorter
shorter.plain: The element is a little narrower than its column; the column keeps its size and stays as it was.

compact.name: compact
compact.plain: The element is narrower still, its title lines and strip on a few lines; the column keeps its size.

tight.name: most compact
tight.plain: The narrowest the element still reads at: its parts wrap onto more lines; the column keeps its size.

act._about: L-36: the hover of every icon on the bench is a verb and its object, nothing more; the roles keep the line that says what the role is.

width.verb: set the width of the element to

copy.obj: this column's settings as one line

in.plain: The shape FastAPI reads the request's body into.

out.plain: The shape the reply's body is built from.

in-nested.plain: A shape inside the request body.

act.name: tests it
act.plain: It sends this request to test it; what it checks on the answer is what it proves.

check.name: sets up and checks
check.plain: It sends this request to set something up, and checks the status it gets.

arrange.name: sets up
arrange.plain: It sends this request only to set something up for a later request.

service.name: from the service side
service.plain: It never sends this request: it calls the code behind it and checks what that code raises.

helper.name: through a helper
helper.plain: A helper it calls sends this request to set something up.

limiter.name: rate limiter
limiter.plain: Counts the requests from one caller and says no when there are too many.

scheme.name: login scheme
scheme.plain: Reads the login header before any code of the endpoint runs.

login.name: login check
login.plain: The dependency that checks who is calling.

rule.name: field rule
rule.plain: A rule on one field of the body; breaking it answers with a list of what is wrong.

own.name: own check
own.plain: A check written in the handler itself.

down.name: check one call down
down.plain: A check inside a function the handler calls.

branch.name: branch that picks the answer
branch.plain: A fork in a called function that decides which answer comes back.

catch.name: catch
catch.plain: An except: an error a call raised is caught here, then turned into an ending, passed on or swallowed — its effect says which.

switch.name: switch
switch.plain: A setting or a binding that decides which code runs.

icon.name: glyph
icon.plain: The kind of ending, as its glyph.

name.name: words
name.plain: What the ending says to the caller; a rate limiter's ending also names its limit.

stage.name: stage
stage.plain: Where in the request it leaves: at the edge, the gate, the input, the handler or the answer.

count.name: ways

via.name: where

icon.name: glyph
icon.plain: The page's own mark for a test: the Gabe Universe draws no node for a test.

state.name: result

proves.name: endings

role.name: role here

name.name: name
name.plain: The test's name, without its prefix and its case id.

sends.name: headers
sends.plain: The headers its requests here send.

asserts.name: checks
asserts.plain: What it checks on the answer here: the status, and the answer's fields it reads.

icon.name: glyph
icon.plain: The gate's own icon, by its kind, as BY MOMENT draws it: its gate icons option decides both.

role.name: kind
role.plain: What sort of gate it is.

cond.name: condition
cond.plain: What it checks, in plain words; the code as written is said last in its hover.

fn.name: function
fn.plain: The function it runs in, with its role.

level.name: where it decides
level.plain: Where in the request it decides: app-wide, at login, in a dependency, in the handler, or inside a call.

effect.name: effect
effect.plain: What happens when it decides: an ending, a returned answer, an error passed on or swallowed.

count.name: tests
count.plain: How many tests prove its effect.

role.name: role
role.plain: The hook's role in the web app.

fkind.name: kind
fkind.plain: A mutation sends a change; a query reads.

sends.name: request
sends.plain: The endpoint it sends to, with its method.

file.name: file
file.plain: The file the hook lives in.

count.name: reactions
count.plain: How many endings the screen answers in a branch of its own.

icon.name: glyph
icon.plain: The glyph of its kind, as BY MOMENT draws it.

life.name: lifetime
life.plain: How long it lives: gone once the answer is sent, or kept by the server for the next request.

name.name: name
name.plain: The value's name in the code.

ikind.name: kind
ikind.plain: What kind of value it is, in BY MOMENT's words.

kind.plain: One colour for every element of this kind — the station's own colour for the kind.

muted.plain: One colour for every element of this kind, quiet enough to recede.

end.inNone: no check of its own stops it: it leaves at {v}
end.undecl: the route does not declare this status
end.ways: ways through the code to it: {n}

test.checksOnly: checks the status {v}, which no ending of this endpoint is joined to by what it reads

gate.inCatch: an error {v} comes up from a call below
gate.doNone: runs in the framework, before the handler
gate.outNone: its effect is not an ending

hook.outNone: the screen answers no ending in a branch of its own

region._about: D-089, his words on the ending's hover ("the hover should work as it is today … if we hover over the icon of the glyph and the status, it should give a different hover only regarding the glyph and the status. For the items at the end in the last row, each item should have its own hover notice about what it is"): the words the REGION cards (_ae-card.js, CDREG) speak that no other line already says. A part of a block carries a region by data (EX.regions: head · title · items); the title region is the block's own card (D-088), the head region one short card about the glyph and the status, the items region one card per item of the row. `status` names every status an ending of the feed gives (the build stops on one it does not name): the HTTP reason phrase, and a plain line only where the page's own table of refusals (enc.fam.gdc) has none. `way` names a mark of the strip by what it is, its words taken from `terms` (one word per concept); a card never says where on the page it is (P2.1). D-090 gives the other seven kinds the same three regions: `head` and `item` below hold their words.

200.name: OK
200.plain: The request worked and the answer carries the result.

201.name: Created
201.plain: The request worked and something new was created.

202.name: Accepted
202.plain: The request was taken and its work goes on after the answer.

204.name: No Content
204.plain: The request worked and the answer carries no body.

304.name: Not Modified
304.plain: What the caller already holds is still current, so no body is sent.

500.name: Internal Server Error
500.plain: Nothing in the code turned the error into an answer.

region.notTaken: this way does not take it

head._about: D-090, his words ("apply this not only to the endings, but to all the other elements that have a similar structure"): what the HEAD card of each other kind says about its class for THIS element — the glyph and the pill that classifies it (a table's channel, a schema's direction, a function's role, a test's result, a gate's kind, a hook's role, an in-flight value's lifetime). One short line per class, never the kind's plain line (a card keeps those off, P1.1); the rest of the card is the element's own facts. A schema, a function, a gate and a hook say a line for each role the build knows (it stops on one it does not).

schema.in: what the client sends, checked before the handler runs
schema.in-nested: a part of what the client sends, checked with it
schema.out-nested: a part of what the handler answers with

fn.accessor: reads or writes the database itself
fn.caller: reaches the database through the functions it calls
fn.gate: checks something and can stop the request
fn.pure: touches no database and reaches no function that does
fn.none: no role is known for it

gate.limiter: counts a caller's requests and refuses the ones past its limit
gate.scheme: reads the login header before the endpoint's own code runs
gate.login: works out who is calling and refuses a caller it does not know
gate.rule: a rule on one field of the body
gate.own: a check written in the handler itself
gate.down: a check inside a function the handler calls
gate.branch: a fork that picks which answer comes back
gate.catch: catches an error from below, then turns it into an answer or passes it on
gate.switch: a setting or a plugged-in part that decides which code runs

hook.fetcher: sends a request to the server
hook.streamer: its request is a stream: the answer keeps arriving
hook.store: reads or writes state the web app keeps
hook.orchestrator: puts other hooks together, touches no data itself
hook.deriver: works out values from its inputs
hook.none: no role is known for it

item._about: D-090: the words an ITEM card says that no other line already says — a mark of a table's or a schema's strip (what kind of field, a key to another table, a unique key), a check a gate waits for or is, the answer a hook has a branch for, where an in-flight value is read, how a request is sent. A card names its item first (the column, the table, the request, the function) and says what the item is under it.
item.own: answered in a branch of its own

legend._about: D-091 (his: the lab's table block marks a column that can be null and a column that is unique — apply it to the table section and to schemas): what a paler mark and a cornered one mean, said ONCE, under a block's strip — the lab's footer row says "optional" the same way — each entry drawn as the strip draws it and counted over the element's own fields. The hover of an entry is its meaning; the card of a mark says the column's own facts.

opt.name: optional
opt.table: A column that can be null. Its mark is drawn paler.
opt.schema: A field the body or the answer may leave out. Its mark is drawn paler.

uq.name: unique
uq.table: A column a unique key names. Its mark carries a corner at its top right and one at its bottom left, and every column that shares the key carries them.

yn._about: D-091 item 4 (his: for functions, endpoints, gates or any other element, a similar encoding, but maybe in the other corners or with other colours): a yes or no the feed itself records on a kind's marks, offered as an option of that kind's column, off until it is chosen, my pick dashed — never on by default. Built for the three kinds whose marks carry such a fact: a function's write that a commit saves, a test's request that proves an ending, a fork the way takes. `corners` uses the two corners a unique key leaves free; `grey` is another colour. A mark of another nature (a read, a request that only sets up, a check) has no such fact and is never marked.
yn.title: extra mark: {v}

off.name: not marked
off.plain: Every mark of this kind is drawn as it is. Nothing is added.

corners.name: corners
corners.plain: A mark that has the fact gets a corner at its top left and one at its bottom right, the corners a unique key leaves free.

grey.name: grey
grey.plain: A mark that lacks the fact is drawn in grey. A mark that has it keeps its colour.

fn.name: saved by a commit
fn.yes: A commit on a way to the answer saves this write.
fn.no: No commit on any way saves this write.
fn.plain: A table the function writes, by whether a commit saves the write. A table it only reads has no such fact and stays as it is.

test.name: proves an ending
test.yes: The request is matched to an ending the code produces, so the test proves it.
test.no: The request reaches the endpoint without being matched to an ending.
test.plain: A request that tests the endpoint, by whether it proves an ending. A request that only sets up has no such fact and stays as it is.

end.name: fork taken
end.yes: The way to this ending takes this branch.
end.no: The way to this ending does not take this branch.
end.plain: A fork on the way, by whether the way takes it. A check, a call or a switch has no such fact and stays as it is.
